co_dali_area_the.blurb: The Dali Area is a small bouldering zone high on Mt Blue Sky, formerly Mt Evans, at roughly 11,100 feet. The 27 problems run from V0 up to a few V12 to V14 testpieces, though most fall between V0 and V5. The rock is clean quartzite with crimps, knobs, flakes and slopers, and the main boulder is steep enough that its south-facing wall often stays shaded in summer. Landings are on talus, so bring several pads. The style rewards finger strength. Easier problems make it a fair stop for mid-grade climbers, while the top end draws strong boulderers.
co_dali_area_the.approach: From the Seurat boulder, follow the trail across the hillside for about 50 yards, then cut back hard and head steeply uphill in the trees to reach the boulder's west side; the landings are ringed by talus.

co_hoosier_pass_lincoln_fall.blurb: Lincoln Falls is a winter ice and mixed venue on the northeast side of Mt Lincoln, just south of Hoosier Pass above Montgomery Reservoir, within easy reach of Breckenridge and the Front Range. The ice runs from short pillars to three-pitch lines, mostly WI3 to WI5 with a few WI2 slabs, and there are mixed lines from M4 to M7. A popular classic gully gives an approachable multi-pitch outing, and an easy top-rope option exists. Because it forms reliably and is close to the road, it gets busy, so start early and avoid weekends if you can.
co_hoosier_pass_lincoln_fall.parking_note: Park near Montgomery Reservoir, reached by a gravel road that turns west off CO 9 roughly a mile south of Hoosier Pass. The road runs through a neighborhood, so keep driveways and the roadway clear.
co_hoosier_pass_lincoln_fall.approach: Follow the road around the north end of the reservoir and then hike a trail uphill to the base of the ice. Do not cross the reservoir surface.

co_south_slabs_the.blurb: The South Slabs form a broad, smooth granite face on Greyrock, the big dome above Poudre Canyon northwest of Fort Collins. Of its 27 climbs, most are trad, with a few bolted lines and one top-rope. Grades span from 5.5 to 5.12, with a good block of moderates around 5.7 and a larger group in the 5.11 range. Routes tend to be single pitches, a few reaching two or three, on friction-dependent slab where bolts can be sparse. It is a quiet, technical place for people who enjoy careful footwork, and midday can be hot, so mornings are comfortable.

co_east_colfax.blurb: East Colfax is a gneiss sport crag beside Tunnel 6 in Clear Creek Canyon, a short drive from Golden. The wall is around 100 feet tall and holds 27 routes, almost all bolted, plus a few trad lines. Grades start at 5.4 and climb to 5.12, with plenty in the 5.5 to 5.9 range and a solid group of 5.11s for stronger climbers. The easy, well protected slab here makes it a favorite for a first outdoor lead, and low anchors let newer climbers practice cleaning. It fills up on weekends, so weekdays or an early start are best. A small beginner crag sits right next door.

co_crestone.blurb: Crestone is a small bouldering and sport spot at the foot of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains in the San Luis Valley, a couple of minutes from the town of Crestone and its creekside campground. Most of the 26 climbs are boulder problems, from VB-level warm-ups to a few around V6, with a handful of bolted and trad lines beyond them. The boulders are packed closely together, which makes for an easy afternoon of circuits. It is a modest local option rather than a destination, but worth a stop if you are in the valley for the big alpine peaks.
